metadata.title: Non-cognitive skills and social gaps in digital skills: Evidence from ICILS 2018

extraction.outcome_summary: The study used ICILS 2018 data on 40,403 eighth-grade students and analyzed computer and information literacy (CIL) plausible values across participating countries/regions/cities. It estimated fixed-effects linear models with survey and replicate weights, comparing a baseline model to extended models that added three proxies for non-cognitive skills derived from test behavior and questionnaire nonresponse. The proxies were all significant predictors of CIL scores, with response-time decline emerging as the strongest predictor, and they substantially reduced the gender and socioeconomic gaps in digital skills. In contrast, adding these proxies widened the immigrant-native gap, contrary to the authors' hypothesis.
